8808.t: From Proto-Indo-European *albʰós (“white”). Cognates include Latin albus (“white”), Hittite 𒀠𒉺𒀸 (alpas, “cloud”), Umbrian 𐌀𐌋𐌚𐌖 (alfu, “white”) and Middle Welsh elbid (“world”).

8800.t: From ἀλέκτωρ (ăléktōr, “cock, rooster”) + -υών (-uṓn, an obscure suffix also appearing in ἀλκυών (alkuṓn, “kingfisher”)).

8826.t: From ἄμνηστος (ắmnēstos, “forgotten, forgetful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix), ultimately from μνάομαι (mnáomai, “remember”).

8818.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

8830.t: ἀμφι- (amphi-, “amphi-, on two sides”) + βάλλω (bállō, “to throw”).

8883.t: From ἀνδρο- (andro-, “man”) + θείνω (theínō, “to slay”) + -ος (-os). Cognate to Sanskrit नृहन् (nṛhán, nṛghné).

8819.t: From ἀ- (a-, not, without) + μέλω (mélō, “to care”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjective suffix).

8885.t: From ἀνα- (ana-, “an intensifying prefix”) + ἐγείρω (egeírō, “to wake”)

8814.t: From ἀ (ă, “un-”) + μαθ- (măth-, root of μανθάνω (mănthắnō, “to learn”)) + -ία (-ĭ́ā).
